models.title: Slide-On Collar Tag
models.description: A slide-on pet nameplate — the collar strap threads through a slot in the tag, so nothing dangles, jingles, or snags. Set your strap's width and thickness and the tag wraps itself around it; type a name and the plate grows to fit. The name sits flush in the top face and every edge is rounded.

models.description: Holds a 32 mm round metal ID tag flat against a 25 mm biothane collar. The collar runs in a channel along the back, enclosed at both ends. The tag presses in through a round opening in the back 1 mm smaller than it all round and seats flat against a 2 mm lip that leaves a 28 mm window over the engraving; the collar pressed in behind it holds it there. Every edge is rounded, most of all on the side against the dog. Print in TPU, face down, with no supports.

models.title: Flashforge Adventurer 5M Filament Sensor
models.description: Ball-plunger filament runout sensor for the Flashforge Adventurer 5M. Two-piece 64D TPU: a body that slips over the 7 mm print-head boss (held by one M3 self-tapping screw), and a cap that mounts a D2F-01F pin-plunger microswitch with two M2 screws which also fasten the switch through its own mount holes. A ball bearing rides in a 40°-tilted pocket tangent to the 1.75 mm filament surface and drops 0.65 mm when filament runs out, releasing the switch. Top of the body accepts a 4 mm-OD PTFE tube (12 mm grip) with a 45° funnel down to the filament bore.

filament.note: Flex is required — body stretches over the printer boss, M3 and M2 threads self-tap into the walls, and the ball snaps into the cavity through the access channel before the cap is fitted

Each seam is a trapezoidal tongue on one piece + blind pocket on the mate — every piece is pressed straight DOWN to seat and pulled straight UP to release, no drop-in keys. models.title: Under-Desk Cord Protector
models.description: Modular cord cradle that screws to the underside of a desk. The profile drops 3 in straight down, then wraps the outside of a 6 in circle for 135° (90 + 45) so cords leaving the desk are supported through the bend instead of kinked over an edge. 8 mm thick throughout. Each 150 mm segment interlocks with the next through a rib-and-groove joint that follows the whole profile — print as many as your desk is wide. Three screws per segment pass through the vertical wall itself — an angled round recess bored in from the cord side takes a #6 × 5/8 in pan-head screw driven straight up into the desktop, with its head bearing on the 2 mm of plastic left below the desk face, so the outside face stays solid and nothing protrudes into the cord channel. An optional prop finishes the half circle at the cradle's tip and runs straight up to the desk — a narrow beam, a solid full-width panel, or a hex screen — closing the tube and taking the sag out of a long run. It bolts onto the shell with M5 × 8 button heads driven into the plastic, in a half-lap that keeps the joint the same thickness as the rest of the tube, so it goes on after the cords are laid in, and takes the desk screws the same way the wall does — recessed and angled, here toward the outside of the tube so a driver can still reach them once it is closed. Prints standing on the grooved end with no supports.

hardware.label: #6 × 5/8 in pan-head wood screw, per segment
#6 × 5/8 in pan-head wood screw into the desk, per full-width prop (1 per narrow beam)

models.title: Folding Panel Divider
models.description: A room divider printed in one piece, already folded. Eight 240 mm panels are joined edge to edge by interlocking knuckle hinges with the pin printed through the bore — the strip comes off the bed hinged, with no assembly and no hardware. Consecutive panels carry their knuckles on opposite faces, so the run zig-zags open accordion-style and folds back down to one panel wide. It prints standing on end, which puts every hinge bore vertical so the bores come out round with no support; a stacking pair is about 118 × 244 mm of bed and 243 mm tall. Snap joiners along the top and bottom edges let a second strip stack on the first for double height. Panel height and width, thickness, panel count, hinge segment count and running clearance are all adjustable.

models.title: Spool Roller Stand (Dry Box)
models.description: A filament spool roller stand for a 300 × 200 × 240 mm dry box interior, sized around the Bambu Lab 200 mm spool — four lanes wide to fill the box, or a single lane on its own. Every lane runs its own pair of rollers on its own pegs, so every spool unwinds independently. The walls between lanes do the supporting: a 608 presses into each end of a roller, one peg through a wall carries both neighbouring rollers at once, and a 0.5 mm shoulder on the peg holds each roller off the flat wall — no pockets, so the walls print flat with nothing to bridge. Each roller flange tapers at 40° from the wall face down to the running surface, filling the 2 mm between spool and wall, so a spool dropped in has one place to go and no edge to perch on. The roller spacing is solved rather than chosen — asking for the spool to sit 8 mm off the floor is what puts the rollers 156.4 mm apart, with the rims meeting them 42.8° off vertical. Filament leaves the bottom of a spool into a PTFE tube whose mouth is held by a clip just behind the spool, clear of it; the tube runs flat through loops in a round-bottomed groove sunk half the tile's thickness, under the back roller to a second clip tucked behind it, and leaves the tile there for a push-fit bulkhead; a drilling template marks a bulkhead hole at each lane centre, and a second marks the tiles' screw-down holes on the box floor. The floor splits into one dovetailed tile per lane, and the walls split into a left, a centre and a right the same way, so every part fits a 220 mm bed; the four-lane templates print in dovetailed halves, the one-lane ones whole. Screw pads through the lattice let the stand be fixed down, and each wall is one crescent-shaped piece — tall at the back, low through the middle, up again at the front. Walls sit on the floor on full-length V ridges, and are screwed down by three M3s up through the floor — front, middle and back — with the two tiles under a centre wall lapping at each. One hex beam per lane, nested end to end, runs through the top back of the walls, clear of the seated spools, and an M3 screw through the back of each wall locks the wall and both beam ends in it together. Spool size, ride height, lane count, roller and bearing dimensions, the PTFE run and the box are all adjustable.

filament.note: Everything but the pegs. Rollers want a few solid perimeters around the bearing pockets; the spools' weight lands on them.
The pegs — they have a plate of their own.

models.title: Spool Dry Box Module
models.description: A sealed dry box for one 200 mm spool, printed in pieces on a Snapmaker U1 with 75A TPU gaskets printed in place. Two round side walls, the spool's diameter plus 2 mm clearance and 3 mm wall each side, with curved 3 mm panels between them. Going round from the top: the hold-down spring module, the lid, the front panel, the front roller module, the underneath panel, the rear roller module and the back panel. Every panel edge flares out to a ridge that presses into a TPU bead in a groove on a rib round the inside of each wall, and M3 cap screws run through the wall, straight down the middle of the TPU channel, into a boss in the panel's edge. Where a panel meets a module or another panel, a TPU strip printed into its end presses on its neighbour. Work in progress: the spring and roller modules, which bolt between the walls, aren't drawn yet, so their places are gaps.
